# Cleaning Report (Stage B)

*Generated by `src/cleaning_report.py` from the outputs of `src/pipeline.py`.*

- Pipeline run: 2026-11-27T19:44:31+00:00 (UTC)
- Input: `search_list_20261127_notification_list.xlsx` - 1714 rows, SHA-256 `aca3905863a34ea5...`
- Output: 1714 alerts in `data/processed/alerts_clean.csv` (no rows removed) plus bridge tables.

**Principle:** no source value is overwritten. Every cleaned column sits next to a `*_raw` column with the original value, and the untouched export is also stored in the database table `raw_export`.

## Summary of transformations

| step | what changed | why | records affected |
|---|---|---|---|
| Column names | Converted to snake_case (e.g. `Alert submitted by` -> `notifying_country`) | Readable, code-friendly names | all 25 columns |
| Whitespace & encoding | Unicode NFC, non-breaking spaces replaced, repeated spaces/line breaks collapsed, trimmed | Invisible differences split identical values into separate categories | 1694 cells in 10 columns |
| Missing values | Kept as missing (no imputation). `Counterfeit`, `Country of origin` keep the source value 'Unknown' as a category | Imputing brands or names would fabricate data | Brand missing: 52; Name missing: 36 |
| Alert ID validation | Pattern `PREFIX/NNNNN/YY` checked; prefix, sequence, year suffix and case ID extracted | Detect malformed IDs; enable year analysis | 1714 of 1714 valid; 0 duplicates |
| Duplicates | Checked exact rows, alert numbers and case URLs; near-duplicates flagged, not removed | Same product can be notified several times legitimately | 0 removed |
| Product names | Case/spacing normalised, spelling variants merged (explicit list), project product group added | `Shower gel`/`shower gel` were counted separately | 125 records changed (51 beyond whitespace); 231 -> 180 types |
| Country names | Safety Gate labels mapped to display names + ISO2 + EU flag | Shorter labels, joinable with other data | origin relabelled: 149; notifier relabelled: 27 |
| Brand names | Case-, accent- and punctuation-insensitive key; most frequent spelling used as display name | `PARFUMS DE QUALITE'` vs `Parfums de Qualité` | 37 records got a different display spelling; 18 brands had >1 spelling |
| Legal provision | Trailing full stop removed, `Cosmetic Product Regulation` -> `Cosmetic Products Regulation` | 21 variants of mostly the same sentence | 1704 records; 21 -> 13 variants |
| Risk types (multivalued) | Split on comma into `alert_risk_types` | Count each risk without double counting | 4 alerts with 2 risk types |
| Corrective measures | Measure blocks parsed into operator, category, group and date | Free text -> analysable fields | 2027 measures from 1714 alerts; 0 parse failures |
| Dates | Measure dates parsed (dd/mm/yyyy); weekly report and publication dates added from official XML | Export has no date column | 1921 measure dates parsed, 106 'Unknown'; 1714 alerts matched to XML |
| Substances | Rule-based extraction from risk text (Stage C) | Main analytical dimension | 1822 mentions in 1709 alerts |

**Measures dated after the weekly report:** 15 measures in 8 alerts have an entry-into-force date later than the weekly report in which the alert appeared. Possible reasons: measures added in later updates of the alert, or data-entry errors. They are kept as recorded.

## Remaining uncertainties

- The meaning of the alert-number suffix and of the XML `publicationDate` is inferred, not officially documented (see `date_investigation.md`).
- Product groups are a project-defined classification; borderline products (e.g. `Hair and body cream`, `Shower foam and deodorant`) were assigned by first matching rule.
- Brand normalisation cannot detect different brands with the same name, or counterfeit use of a brand name (the official disclaimer warns about this).
- `Unknown` country of origin (267 alerts) means the origin was not established by the notifying authority; these alerts are excluded only from origin-specific percentages, and this is always stated.
- The substance dictionary was built from the texts in this export; new alerts may name substances it does not contain. These surface as 'uncertain candidates'.
